figures.label: fig:2

figures.caption: The oscillatory motion of the particle through its quantum distribution in configuration space is not a simple harmonic motion. For both diagrams, $m=5$. figures.label: fig:3

figures.caption: The motion of the object within its quantum distribution in the gravity-dominant regime. Parameters are set to $R=1$, $m=1$, $\hbar=1$, and $G=1$. The period of oscillation is dependent on the initial position of the object and the width of its associated wave packet.

The period of oscillation is inversely dependent on the mass of the object.

abstracts.value: We present a novel perspective on gravity-induced wave function reduction using Bohmian trajectories. This study examines the quantum motion of both point particles and objects, identifying critical parameters for the transition from quantum to classical regimes. By analyzing the system’s dynamics, we define the reduction time of the wave function through Bohmian trajectories, introducing a fresh viewpoint in this field. Our findings align with results obtained in standard quantum mechanics, confirming the validity of this approach.

We present a novel perspective on gravity-induced wave function reduction using Bohmian trajectories. This study examines the quantum motion of both point particles and objects, identifying critical parameters for the transition from quantum to classical regimes. By analyzing the system's dynamics, we define the reduction time of the wave function through Bohmian trajectories, introducing a fresh viewpoint in this field. Our findings align with results obtained in standard quantum mechanics, confirming the validity of this approach.
